record.issuing_body: Government representatives at the 2023 REAIM summit on responsible AI in the military domain, The Hague, organised by the Netherlands' Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Defence and co-hosted by the Republic of Korea
record.summary: Joint call agreed by government representatives at the 2023 REAIM summit in The Hague on the responsible development, deployment and use of AI in the military domain. It names concerns about unreliable AI systems, human involvement, unclear liability and unintended escalation; commits to keeping humans responsible and accountable for decisions; stresses appropriate safeguards and human oversight, risk assessment and data governance consistent with international law; warns that adoption without sufficient research, testing and assurance may cause inadvertent harm; and invites states to develop national frameworks.
record.notes: Agreed at the first REAIM summit, held at the World Forum in The Hague on 15-16 February 2023, organised by the Dutch foreign and defence ministries and co-hosted by South Korea, with some 2,000 delegates. The text has 25 numbered paragraphs: sixteen on shared understandings of the opportunities and risks of military AI, followed by the call to action proper (paragraphs 17 to 25), which asks states, the private sector, academia and civil society to build knowledge, exchange good practices and continue a multi-stakeholder dialogue, and ends by inviting all stakeholders worldwide to join it. The government's list of endorsing countries and territories (published 4 April 2025) names 58, among them China, the United States, the Netherlands and the Republic of Korea. The summit also announced a Global Commission on AI in the military domain. Later REAIM summits produced the Blueprint for Action (Seoul, 2024; INT-16) and the 2026 Pathways to Action (INT-18), which builds on both.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the government.nl publication page of 16 February 2023 and the 4-page PDF of the Call to Action; the government.nl news item of 16 February 2023 on the agreement (organisers, co-host, some 2,000 delegates, the Global Commission); the announcement of 19 January 2023 (World Forum, The Hague, 15 and 16 February 2023); the 2-page list of endorsing countries and territories (58 names; its document page is dated 04-04-2025); and the REAIM 2026 Pathways to Action PDF, which names the 2023 Call to Action and the 2024 Blueprint. Together they confirm the title, the date, the issuing body and the full text summarised.

judgment.status_reasoning: A political call to action agreed on 16 February 2023 and open to further endorsement ('We invite all stakeholders worldwide to join this Call to Action'); nothing stored withdraws or replaces it, and the later REAIM documents build on it. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.date_reasoning: government.nl gives the publication date 16-02-2023 for the Call to Action; the PDF itself carries no date.
